description: TestNest is a seed-stage startup founded by an experienced team of embedded systems and software engineers with backgrounds in automotive, telecommunications, IoT, and space sectors. The company aims to transform the way CubeSat systems are verified and validated before launch through an innovative test automation and emulation platform. The core product – the Virtual Orbital Lab (VOL) – emulates satellite sensors and orbital conditions, enabling developers to test real flight hardware under realistic mission scenarios on Earth. This Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) approach allows continuous validation of firmware and subsystem interactions, introducing Continuous Integration (CI)practices into space engineering. Operating in the upstream domain, TestNest’s innovation reduces development costs, shortens test cycles, and enhances mission reliability. By enabling early detection of design and integration issues, the platform helps CubeSat developers, research institutions, and commercial operators achieve higher mission success rates, ultimately contributing to safer and more efficient access to space.

description: TRACK is a digital hiking system that combines an app, a wearable safety device (ALINA), and a backend platform to merge immersive audio experiences with proactive safety while being independent of mobile coverage. The TRACK app acts as a hands-free audio guide that plays curated content triggered by GNSS signals, while the ALINA device provides precise and robust positioning using the Galileo High Accuracy Service (HAS), predictive location estimation in case of signal loss, and automatic emergency detection. Within incubation, the focus lies on the ALINA device: building and testing hardware prototypes (alpha to market-ready), integrating Galileo HAS, and ensuring seamless interaction between app, device and backend including CE preparation. The predictive algorithms that enable trajectory modelling and fall detection are developed separately under the ALINA Core R&D project and only integrated into the device. TRACK addresses hikers, destinations, and rescue organisations seeking safer and more sustainable outdoor experiences. By bringing sub-metre Galileo HAS precision to consumer-grade equipment, TRACK demonstrates a clear downstream use of space technology, turning satellite accuracy and resilience into tangible value on the trail.

These insoles enable caregivers and family members to locate and assist individuals in real time, ensuring their safety while allowing them to maintain independence in everyday life. The business operates in the health and assistive technology domain, bridging innovation between healthcare, digitalization, and mobility. Its solution leverages spacebased satellite navigation (GNSS) to provide precise and reliable location tracking, even in challenging environments. This downstream use of space technology ensures accurate positioning, a crucial factor for emergency response and continuous monitoring. By combining medical insight with advanced space data, Clever Sole creates a unique safety ecosystem that empowers individuals with dementia and relieves caregivers from constant supervision. The innovation demonstrates how space technology can serve humanity in practical, socially meaningful ways.
